pair_timing.reason: both candidates miss the frozen 1.22x single-Gate stop-loss

k64_log.expected_exit: nonzero solely because 1.017890x misses the 1.22x single-Gate requirement after every timing round and every non-performance gate pass

static_sass.scope: production, K16, and K64 C512 Gate function blocks
static_sass.interpretation: register feeding removes static decoded-B shared-memory and control instructions without changing the 16 HMMA operations or introducing spills, but K16 loses performance and K64 recovers only 1.789% throughput

stop_loss_and_skipped_work.trigger: K16 regresses to 0.953168x; K64 improves every round but reaches only 1.017890x against the frozen 1.22x gate

decision.result: reject production integration and close the single-branch register-fed sidecar line
closed_scope: K16-granular fragment-native equal-byte Gate/Up sidecars with direct WMMA B-fragment feed
K64-vectorized equal-byte Gate/Up sidecars with direct WMMA B-fragment feed
further micro-tuning of this unchanged single-branch M128 register-fed arithmetic body
decision.reason: K64 prefetch converts a 4.68% throughput regression into only a 1.789% gain, leaving roughly 20 percentage points to the admission gate and providing no basis for a 5.9766-GiB full-model sidecar allocation
decision.canonical_plus_shuffle_assessment: not implemented: returning to canonical layout would reintroduce gather/shuffle work that the equal-byte fragment-native layouts removed, so it has less credible ceiling than the rejected K64 bound and is not the next probe

next_priority.mechanism: test-only 512-thread M128 fused Gate+Up kernel using canonical weights and one shared-A stage across both projections
next_priority.rationale: the next candidate must reuse activation and reduce the pair boundary rather than optimize the now-bounded single-branch B feed

decision.bulk_attention_status: already production-integrated and only 2.904% of the current profile

reproduction.environment_requirement: run under MAXN with CPU 0, GPU 1300500000 Hz, and EMC 3200000000 Hz read back before accepting timings

limitations: The Gate/Up payload is deterministic and checkpoint-like rather than loaded checkpoint tensor bytes.
The sidecar builder is excluded from timing and the microbenchmark retains canonical tensors for comparison.
Only isolated single-Gate eager timing was admitted; no pair, Graph-timing, whole-layer, whole-model, API, or EvalScope performance follows.
No NCU or Nsys capture was run, so static SASS counts are structural evidence rather than measured traffic or stall attribution.
The rejection closes these two sidecar granularities and this single-branch register-fed body, not every possible fused Gate/Up dataflow.
